issue: What standard of appellate review applies to an unpreserved challenge to the sufficiency of the evidence in a criminal case: the miscarriage-of-justice/devoid-of-evidence test, or plain-error review under Olano?
provision: Fed. R. Crim. P. 52(b); Jackson v. Virginia, 443 U.S. 307 (1979); Olano (United States v. Olano, 507 U.S. 725 (1993))

sides.position: Unpreserved sufficiency-of-the-evidence claims are reviewed under the miscarriage-of-justice/devoid-of-evidence standard, which predates Jackson.
cases: United States v. Burris, 999 F.3d 973 (6th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Delgado, 672 F.3d 320 (6th Cir. 2012) (en banc)
United States v. Williams, 784 F.3d 798 (D.C. Cir. 2015)
United States v. Turner, 551 F.3d 657 (7th Cir. 2008)

sides.position: Unpreserved sufficiency-of-the-evidence claims are reviewed under the more stringent plain-error standard (Olano), or under the Jackson standard, rather than the devoid-of-evidence test.
cases: United States v. Wolfe, 245 F.3d 257 (3d Cir. 2001)

quote: Because this standard predates Jackson and runs afoul of Olano’s instructions involving plain-error review, we are concerned that our court may have chosen the wrong side of this circuit split.
cite: United States v. Sirshun Burris, 999 F.3d 973 (6th Cir. 2021)
